source_user: A team wants lower serving cost through weight-only quantization. Define a fair comparison. Scenario variant 299: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.
corrected_answer: For scenario variant 299, define the estimand before testing: change in cost per successful output token at each fixed offered load, with quality and reliability gates. Assume one named model checkpoint, tokenizer, prompt/request trace, decoding policy, hardware, driver, runtime, scheduler, batching/cache policy, power limits, and software build are frozen; vary only the weight-only quantization configuration. Document bit width, group size, scales, outlier handling, calibration-set provenance, kernel support, and any fallback. Preregister a falsifiable hypothesis with a numerical target (for example, a specified cost reduction) and non-inferiority margins for task quality, safety/correctness, TTFT, TPOT, error rate, and p99 latency. Keep calibration and held-out sets disjoint. Randomize interleaved baseline/treatment trials using identical requests after equal warm-up and compilation, with a fixed sample size, exclusion rule, stopping rule, and confidence-interval method. Record quality scores, memory in GiB, TTFT/TPOT in ms, completed tokens/s, concurrency, utilization, energy, fully loaded cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, timeouts, OOMs, kernel fallbacks, retries, and cleanup failures with per-request raw data and units. Stratify by prompt length, output length, concurrency, and cache state; report paired estimates and uncertainty rather than averages alone. Abort and restore the versioned baseline on quality or safety regression, excess tail latency, instability, unauthorized data exposure, or unrecoverable resource leakage. Evidence required: signed configuration and authorization, calibration/held-out manifests, raw logs, fallback/failure records, confidence intervals, and a tested rollback runbook; do not infer platform-specific support without measurement.
risks: unsupported kernels or silent fallback may make the comparison invalid
thermal drift, cache state, scheduler and load mix can bias latency and cost
finite held-out coverage may miss quality, safety or rare reliability regressions
evidence_required: versioned configuration, authorization, and reversible rollback plan
disjoint tuning/calibration and held-out evaluation manifests
randomized paired raw metrics with units and confidence intervals
failure, cleanup/recovery, redaction, and isolation records

source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 1: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer: For scenario variant 1, choose tensor or pipeline parallelism only after specifying the latency SLA, model/checkpoint and sequence-length distribution, batch/concurrency target, GPU count/type, interconnect topology, memory budget, runtime support, availability objective, and whether reconfiguration is allowed. State the falsifiable hypothesis as a numerical comparison, such as which design yields lower p99 end-to-end latency at a declared throughput while meeting quality, error-rate, and memory gates. Freeze model, software, drivers, placement, request mix, decoding, power limits, and load generator; vary only the parallelism strategy and its preregistered partition/microbatch settings. Measure per-GPU memory and utilization, communication bytes and time, synchronization waits, pipeline bubbles, queueing, TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput in requests/s and tokens/s, energy/cost, errors, timeouts, OOMs, stragglers, failed-rank recovery, and reconfiguration time. Use randomized interleaved trials with identical requests, equal warm-up, disjoint tuning and evaluation workloads, fixed sample size and confidence intervals. Analyze by sequence length, batch size, concurrency, topology and failure injection; explain tensor collectives versus pipeline stage imbalance and microbatch effects rather than attributing correlation to the strategy. Enforce authorization and isolation, redact request data, and roll back to the last known-good placement when SLA, safety, correctness, availability, or data-isolation gates fail. Evidence required: topology and version manifest, partition/microbatch configuration, raw synchronized per-request and per-rank traces, failure/recovery logs, uncertainty estimates, and a rehearsed rollback/reconfiguration procedure.
risks: communication topology, stage imbalance and microbatching can confound the strategy effect
warm-up, queueing, cache state and thermal or placement drift can bias tail latency
failure-injection and held-out workload coverage may not represent production incidents
evidence_required: versioned configuration, authorization, and reversible rollback plan
